issues.description: The script uses XMLHttpRequest to fetch and execute remote code via a[a][a](x.responseText), which is equivalent to eval(). The URL is arbitrary (passed to loadModule), allowing remote code execution.
issues.recommendation: Remove dynamic code execution and only use static, trusted code. Never eval or execute fetched code from arbitrary URLs.

issues.description: The script uses a[a][a](x.responseText), which is a highly obfuscated way to call eval().
issues.recommendation: Avoid obfuscation and use clear, maintainable code. Remove any use of eval or similar constructs.

issues.description: The script requests and executes code from arbitrary URLs via loadModule, which can be used to exfiltrate data or execute malicious code.
issues.recommendation: Restrict network requests to trusted domains and avoid executing fetched code.

issues.description: The script stores a unique user identifier (UUID) in persistent storage (GM.setValue('id', uuidv4())), which can be used for tracking.
issues.location: Anonymous async IIFE near top of script
issues.recommendation: Do not generate or store persistent unique identifiers unless absolutely necessary and with user consent.

issues.description: The script applies to a wide range of high-value targets (Discord, Facebook, Google, Baidu, etc.), increasing the risk of privilege abuse and data exposure.
issues.recommendation: Limit script scope to only necessary domains.

issues.description: The script requests high-privilege grants (unsafeWindow, GM_getTabs, GM_saveTab, etc.), but not all are used in the visible code.
issues.recommendation: Only request the minimum necessary permissions.

issues.description: The script uses @require to load third-party libraries from GreasyFork and jQuery from code.jquery.com, but does not pin versions with hashes.
issues.recommendation: Pin all third-party dependencies to specific versions and use trusted CDNs.

issues.description: The script uses innerHTML/outerHTML in some utility functions (not fully visible in the snippet), and the use of eval-like constructs increases XSS risk.
issues.location: Utils.loadModule and possible other dynamic code paths
issues.recommendation: Sanitize all user input and avoid inserting untrusted content into the DOM.
